Secondary batteries · Commercial

Lead-acid batteries

Both electrodes become lead sulfate during discharge, producing power. Charging restores the original materials.

Animated operating principles

Ion and electron pathways

H⁺ / SO₄²⁻ · electrolyte / membrane Electrons e⁻ · external circuit

Simplified reaction directions and pathways. Actual particle numbers and speeds differ.

Electrode and electrolyte principles

Aqueous sulfuric acid. Discharge consumes acid and forms water.

Overall discharge: Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄ → 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O

Advantages

Low initial cost, high short-term power and established recycling

Drawbacks & challenges

Heavy, with limited energy density and deep-discharge cycle life. Lead and acid require management.

Materials & supply constraints

Lead is not a rare earth; toxicity and recycling management are key.

Main applications

Vehicle starting, UPS and telecom backup
